title: Hidden Members; The First Man Clothed for War
description: T61 unfolds the body's hidden and visible members as a sustained correspondence: as the body has interior organs hidden and untouched in their fullness within, and other members openly visible at the surface, so the Lord stays hidden in his inmost — divine love in its own dominion — while two great vessels of his shining go forth as the eyes openly manifest, and the tongue speaks from within proclaiming the body's glory and shame, its wound and its healing. T62 describes the Divine Human, clothed in the elements, standing firm against the first opposition of the proprium. Into that contest love and thought are given over; the outer covering of the strong loves is let fall, the proprium swallows them, and they break open from within — a river of falsity pours from the proprium's mouth, a branch of the great river of judgment that they bear in themselves.
